stem:
Megha leaves cut fruit uncovered on a plate. She also stores mango pickle and murabba made with enough salt or sugar.

Which claim correctly explains the difference?

options.text: Microorganisms from the surroundings can infect the uncovered fruit, but enough salt or sugar in the pickle and murabba stops those organisms from growing.
Even a tiny pinch of salt or sugar is enough to stop microorganisms from infecting any food.
The fruit rots first, and that rotting then produces the microorganisms.
Food left open only to air cannot rot, because microorganisms live only in water and soil.

teacher.key_rationale: Microbes in the surroundings can spoil exposed food; high salt or sugar blocks infection. A tiny amount is not enough, rotting does not create the microbes first, and microbes are not limited to water and soil.
